question: Under the amended AI Act, when may providers process special categories of personal data for bias detection?
judge_reason: It gives the strict-necessity rule and accurately summarizes most safeguards, but omits the required appropriate safeguards for fundamental rights and freedoms and overstates that all paragraph 1 conditions apply to other systems and models.
baseline_judge_reason: The answer states that high-risk AI providers may process special-category data for bias detection and correction only when strictly necessary and with fundamental-rights safeguards, and adds no apparent contradiction.
answer:
Providers may exceptionally process special-category personal data for bias detection and correction only “to the extent strictly necessary.” For providers of high-risk AI systems, the processing must also meet all the safeguards and conditions in Article 4a(1): other data, including synthetic or anonymised data, cannot effectively serve the purpose; access and reuse must be tightly limited and protected; the data cannot be made accessible to other parties; it must be deleted once the bias is corrected or the retention period ends; and the necessity must be documented. [AI Act Art. 4a(1)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02024R1689-20260727#art_4a)

Providers of other AI systems or models may do so only where the potential bias is likely to affect health or safety, negatively affect fundamental rights, or lead to discrimination prohibited under Union law—and they must apply all the conditions and safeguards in Article 4a(1). Use **layered defenses** against prompt injection:

- Treat user-provided, retrieved, and external content as **untrusted data**, and instruct the model not to let it override its task or reveal sensitive information. [AML.M0021](https://atlas.mitre.org/mitigations/AML.M0021)

- Conduct recurring, authorized red-team exercises to find and remediate weaknesses across the whole AI-enabled system. [AML.M0035](https://atlas.mitre.org/mitigations/AML.M0035)
- Log model inputs and outputs, and, for agents, intermediate decisions, data access, and tool use so activity can be monitored. [AML.M0024](https://atlas.mitre.org/mitigations/AML.M0024)
